subject: physics
title: Orbits and Kepler's Third Law
welcome_lead: Balance gravity with centripetal force to derive T² ∝ r³.
meta_desc: A-Level Gravitational Fields adventure on circular orbits and Kepler's third law.
final_note: Geostationary satellites orbit Earth in exactly 24 hours at ~42,000 km radius.

concepts.def: Passes over both poles, low altitude usual.

walkthroughs.body_html: G M m / r² = m v² / r. Cancel m, rearrange: v² = G M / r, so v = √(GM/r). Higher orbits are slower.
Substitute v = 2π r / T into v² = GM/r. Result: T² ∝ r³. Bigger orbits take much longer (cube root squared relation).
Set T = 24 h = 86,400 s, solve r ≈ 4.2 × 10⁷ m (above equator). Satellite stays above one spot on Earth — perfect for TV and weather.
